name: 0-polygraph
quote: A 0-polygraph is simply another name for a set.

name: 1-polygraph
quote: A 1-polygraph 𝑃 consists of a 0-polygraph 𝑃0 ... together with a set 𝑃1 of 1-generators and two functions 𝑠0𝑃, 𝑡0𝑃 : 𝑃1 → 𝑃0

name: graph (1-polygraph = directed multigraph)
quote: The notion of 1-polygraph is simply another name for the notion of graph, by which we always mean a directed multigraph

name: morphism of 1-polygraphs / category Pol1
quote: We write Pol1 for the category of 1-polygraphs and their morphisms.

name: P-congruence and presented set

data.congruence: smallest equivalence relation ≈P on P0 with x≈P y for a:x→y in P1

quote: The 𝑃-congruence ≈ 𝑃 associated with a 1-polygraph 𝑃 is the smallest equivalence relation on 𝑃0 such that 𝑥 ≈ 𝑃 𝑦 for every 1-generator 𝑎 : 𝑥 → 𝑦

name: abstract rewriting system (terminology)
quote: they give it yet another name and call it an abstract rewriting system. In this context, the elements of 𝑃0 are called objects and those of 𝑃1 are called rewriting rules

name: normal form / normal form properties
quote: A 0-cell 𝑥 ∈ 𝑃0 is a normal form when there is no rule 𝑎 : 𝑥 → 𝑦 in 𝑃1 with 𝑥 as source.

name: termination
quote: A 1-polygraph 𝑃 is terminating (or well-founded or noetherian or strongly normalizing) when there is no infinite sequence of rewriting steps

name: branching

data.branching: pair (f,f') of coinitial rewriting paths f:x→*y, f':x→*y'

quote: a pair ( 𝑓 , 𝑓 ′ ) of coinitial rewriting paths 𝑓 : 𝑥 →∗ 𝑦 and 𝑓 ′ : 𝑥 →∗ 𝑦 ′ is called a branching. The 0-cell 𝑥 is called the source of the branching.

name: confluence

data.confluent_branching: (f,f') confluent when targets y,y' are joinable

quote: A branching ( 𝑓 , 𝑓 ′ ) as above is confluent when 𝑦 and 𝑦 ′ are joinable ... A 1-polygraph is confluent (resp. locally confluent) when every branching (resp. local branching) is confluent.

name: Newman's lemma
quote: A terminating 1-polygraph is confluent if and only if it is locally confluent.

name: convergence
quote: A 1-polygraph is convergent when it is both terminating and confluent.

name: free category on a 1-polygraph (P*)
quote: A 1-polygraph 𝑃 induces a category 𝑃∗, called the category freely generated by 𝑃, or the free category on 𝑃

name: free groupoid on a 1-polygraph (P⊤)

data.morphisms: composable sequences of forward/backward 1-generators, quotiented by cancellation

quote: we write 𝑃⊤ for the free groupoid on the category 𝑃∗ ... morphisms from 𝑥 to 𝑦 are composable sequences [of forward or backward 1-generators]

name: 2-polygraph
quote: A 2-polygraph consists of ... a set 𝑃2 of 2-generators together with two functions 𝑠1, 𝑡1 : 𝑃2 → 𝑃1∗, associating to each relation its source and target

name: 2-cells as rewriting rules (2-generator)

data.generator: α : u ⇒ v with s1(α)=u, t1(α)=v, u,v ∈ P1*

quote: We often write 𝛼 : 𝑢 ⇒ 𝑣 for a 2-generator 𝛼 in 𝑃2 such that 𝑠1 (𝛼) = 𝑢 and 𝑡1 (𝛼) = 𝑣

name: presented category

data.P_congruence: smallest congruence ≈P on P* with u≈P v for α:u⇒v in P2

quote: The category 𝑃 presented by a 2-polygraph 𝑃 is the category 𝑃 = 𝑃∗⩽1 /≈ 𝑃 obtained by quotienting the category freely generated by the underlying polygraph by the 𝑃-congruence, what we usually write 𝑃∗⩽1 /𝑃2.

name: 2-graph / 2-globular set
quote: A 2-graph 𝐶, or 2-globular set, ... such that 𝑠0 ◦ 𝑠1 = 𝑠0 ◦ 𝑡1, 𝑡0 ◦ 𝑠1 = 𝑡0 ◦ 𝑡1

name: 2-category
quote: A 2-category consists in a 2-graph 𝐶 together with ... a horizontal composite 1-cell 𝑓 ∗0 𝑔 : 𝑥 → 𝑧 ... a vertical composite 2-cell 𝛼 ∗1 𝛽 : 𝑓 ⇒ ℎ : 𝑥 → 𝑦

name: interchange law (exchange law)
quote: the exchange law holds: given 1-cells 𝑓 : 𝑥 → 𝑦 and 𝑔 : 𝑦 → 𝑧, one has 1 𝑓 ∗0 1𝑔 = 1 𝑓 ∗0 𝑔

name: whiskering (omission notation for identities/∗0)

data.shorthand: u α w * β written instead of (1u *0 α *0 1w) *1 β

quote: we often omit writing identities and horizontal compositions ∗0, and write ∗ for vertical composition ∗1: for instance, we write 𝑢𝛼𝑤 ∗ 𝛽 instead of (1𝑢 ∗0 𝛼 ∗0 1𝑤 ) ∗1 𝛽

name: whisker / context of a rewriting step

data.context: the pair (u,w) of 1-cells flanking a rewriting step u α w : uvw ⇒ uv'w

quote: The pair (𝑢, 𝑤) of 1-cells in 𝑃1∗ is sometimes called the context or whisker in which the rule 𝛼 applies to the 1-cell 𝑢𝑣𝑤.

name: free 2-category on a 2-polygraph (P*)

data.C2: smallest set containing P2, closed under *0 and *1, quotiented by 2-category axioms

quote: The free 2-category 𝑃∗ generated by a 2-polygraph 𝑃 is the 2-category 𝐶 with 𝑃∗⩽1 as underlying category ... whose 2-cells are freely generated by 𝑃2

name: string diagrams

data.2_cells: points/boxes with input wires above, output wires below

quote: 0-cells are pictured as 2-dimensional region of the plane, 1-cells are pictured as wires and 2-cells are pictured as points

name: theorem: string diagrams present the free 2-category
quote: String diagrams (up to planar isotopy) are the 2-cells of a 2-category which is the free 2-category 𝑃∗ on the 2-polygraph 𝑃.

name: critical branching classification: trivial branching
quote: A branching (𝜙1 , 𝜙2 ) : 𝑢 ⇒ (𝑣1 , 𝑣2 ) is trivial when 𝜙1 = 𝜙2.

name: critical branching classification: orthogonal branching

data.shape: u=u1 v u2 w u3, φ1=u1 α u2 w u3, φ2=u1 v u2 β u3

quote: A local branching (𝜙1 , 𝜙2 ) : 𝑢 ⇒ (𝑣1 , 𝑣2 ) is orthogonal when it is of the form 𝑢 = 𝑢1 𝑣𝑢2 𝑤𝑢3 , 𝜙1 = 𝑢1 𝛼𝑢2 𝑤𝑢3 , 𝜙2 = 𝑢1 𝑣𝑢2 𝛽𝑢3

name: critical branching classification: overlapping / minimal / critical

data.order: (φ1,φ2) ⊑ (φ1',φ2') when φi' = u φi w for context (u,w)

quote: A local branching is critical when it is overlapping and minimal.

name: critical branching lemma

data.statement: P locally confluent iff all critical branchings of P are confluent

quote: A 2-polygraph is locally confluent if and only if all its critical branchings are confluent.

name: finiteness of critical branchings
quote: Given a 2-polygraph 𝑃 with a finite set 𝑃2 of rewriting rules, the number of critical branchings is finite.

name: 3-polygraph

data.P3: 3-generators, a cellular extension of the free 2-category P* generated by P

quote: A 3-polygraph (𝑃, 𝑃3) consists of a 2-polygraph 𝑃 together with a cellular extension 𝑃3 of the 2-category 𝑃∗ freely generated by 𝑃, the elements of 𝑃3 being referred to as 3-generators.

name: globular identities (general statement)

data.pattern: for the n-truncation of an (n+1)-polygraph, s*n∘s(n+1) = s*n∘t(n+1) and t*n∘s(n+1) = t*n∘t(n+1)

quote: the globular identities are satisfied: 𝑠∗𝑛 ∘ 𝑠𝑛+1 = 𝑠∗𝑛 ∘ 𝑡𝑛+1 and 𝑡∗𝑛 ∘ 𝑠𝑛+1 = 𝑡∗𝑛 ∘ 𝑡𝑛+1

name: presented 2-category (dimension 3)
quote: The 2-category presented by 𝑃 is the 2-category, denoted by 𝑃, obtained by quotienting the free 2-category over 𝑃 ⩽2 by the congruence ≈ 𝑃 generated by 𝑃3 on 2-cells ... 𝑃 = 𝑃∗⩽2 /𝑃3

name: (n,p)-polygraph — the (3,1)-polygraph instance

data.p: 1 (dimension above which cells are freely invertible)
data.P3: cellular extension of the free (2,1)-category P⊤ (2-cells of P⊤ invertible)

quote: A (3, 1)-polygraph is a pair (𝑃, 𝑃3) consisting of a 2-polygraph 𝑃 and a cellular extension 𝑃3 of the free (2, 1)-category 𝑃⊤.

name: cellular extension / 2-sphere

data.cellular_extension: a set X with maps s2,t2 : X→C2 landing on 2-spheres of C

quote: A cellular extension of 𝐶 is a set 𝑋 equipped with two maps 𝑠2 , 𝑡2 : 𝑋 → 𝐶2 such that, for every 𝐴 in 𝑋, the pair (𝑠2 ( 𝐴), 𝑡2 ( 𝐴)) is a 2-sphere of 𝐶.

name: acyclic extension

data.condition: φ ≈X ψ holds for every 2-sphere (φ,ψ) of C
data.alt_name: homotopy basis (Squier: ≈X is a homotopy relation)

quote: we say that a cellular extension 𝑋 of a 2-category 𝐶 is acyclic, or equivalently that 𝐶 is 𝑋-acyclic, if 𝜙 ≈𝑋 𝜓 holds for every 2-sphere (𝜙, 𝜓) of 𝐶.

name: coherent presentation

data.coherent_(3,1)-polygraph: P3 is an acyclic extension of the free (2,1)-category P⊤_{≤2}
data.extended_presentation: (3,1)-polygraph P whose underlying 2-polygraph P_{≤2} presents C
data.coherent_presentation: an extended presentation that is coherent

quote: A (3, 1)-polygraph 𝑃 is coherent when 𝑃3 is an acyclic extension of the free (2, 1)-category 𝑃⊤⩽2 ... A coherent presentation of 𝐶 is an extended presentation 𝑃 of 𝐶 which is coherent.

name: Squier's homotopical theorem (coherence by convergence)

data.hypothesis: P a convergent 2-polygraph; P3 contains one generating-confluence 3-generator per critical branching of P

quote: If 𝑃3 contains, for every critical branching (𝜙, 𝜓) of 𝑃, one 3-generator ... then the (3, 1)-polygraph (𝑃, 𝑃3) is coherent.

name: generating confluence

data.shape: 3-generator A : φ ∗1 φ'^{-1} ⇛ ψ ∗1 ψ'^{-1} indexed by a critical branching (φ,ψ)

quote: A 3-generator of the form (7.2), indexed by a critical branching of 𝑃, is called a generating confluence of the polygraph 𝑃.

name: Example 1.1.2 — small 1-polygraph
quote: 𝑃 = ⟨ 𝑥, 𝑦, 𝑧 | 𝑎 : 𝑥 → 𝑦, 𝑏 : 𝑥 → 𝑦, 𝑐 : 𝑦 → 𝑦 ⟩

name: Example 2.3.7 — symmetric group Sn presentation

data.P2: a_i a_i ⇒ 1; a_i a_(i+1) a_i ⇒ a_(i+1) a_i a_(i+1); a_i a_j ⇒ a_j a_i for i+1<j

quote: 𝑎 𝑖 𝑎 𝑖 ⇒ 1, for 0 ⩽ 𝑖 < 𝑛 ... 𝑎 𝑖 𝑎 𝑖+1 𝑎 𝑖 ⇒ 𝑎 𝑖+1 𝑎 𝑖 𝑎 𝑖+1 ... 𝑎 𝑖 𝑎 𝑗 ⇒ 𝑎 𝑗 𝑎 𝑖 , for 0 ⩽ 𝑖 < 𝑗 < 𝑛 with 𝑖 + 1 < 𝑗

name: Example 2.3.12 — walking isomorphism
quote: 𝑃 = 𝑥, 𝑦 𝑎 : 𝑥 → 𝑦, 𝑏 : 𝑦 → 𝑥 𝛼 : 𝑎𝑏 ⇒ 1 𝑥 , 𝛽 : 𝑏𝑎 ⇒ 1 𝑦

name: Example 4.3.1 / 4.3.12 — single-generator idempotent monoid

data.critical_branchings: one, (αa, aα) on source aaa, confluent
data.properties: terminating (length decreases) and confluent, hence convergent

quote: 𝑃 = ⟨ ⋆ | 𝑎 | 𝛼 : 𝑎𝑎 ⇒ 𝑎 ⟩

name: Example 4.3.11 — non-locally-confluent 2-polygraph
quote: 𝑃 = ⟨ ⋆ | 𝑎, 𝑏, 𝑐 | 𝛼 : 𝑎𝑏𝑐 ⇒ 𝑎, 𝛽 : 𝑐𝑎 ⇒ 𝑎 ⟩

name: Example 4.3.13 — free group presentation

data.P2: {λ_a: a a-bar⇒1, ρ_a: a-bar a⇒1 : a in X}
data.properties: locally confluent, terminating (length-decreasing), hence convergent; normal forms are reduced words

quote: 𝑃 = ⟨ ⋆ | 𝑎, 𝑎 | 𝜆 : 𝑎𝑎 ⇒ 1, 𝜌 : 𝑎𝑎 ⇒ 1 ⟩ 𝑎∈𝑋

name: Example 10.1.2 — Mon, the 3-polygraph for monoids

data.P3: {A: (μ∗0a)∗1μ ⇛ (a∗0μ)∗1μ  (associativity); L: (η∗0a)∗1μ ⇛ a  (left unit); R: (a∗0η)∗1μ ⇛ a  (right unit)}

quote: Mon = ⟨ ⋆ | 𝑎 | 𝜇 : 𝑎 ∗0 𝑎 ⇒ 𝑎, 𝜂 : 1⋆ ⇒ 𝑎 | 𝐴, 𝐿, 𝑅 ⟩

name: Example 7.2.2 — coherent (3,1)-polygraph for the idempotent monoid
quote: ⟨ ⋆ | 𝑎 | 𝛼 : 𝑎𝑎 ⇒ 𝑎 | 𝐴 : 𝑎𝛼 ∗ 𝛼 ⇛ 𝛼𝑎 ∗ 𝛼 ⟩

name: Example 7.3.6 — generating confluence produced by Squier's theorem

data.P3: {A: αa ∗1 α ⇛ aα ∗1 α, the generating confluence for the unique critical branching}

quote: By Theorem 7.3.5, the (3, 1)-polygraph ⟨ ⋆ | 𝑎 | 𝛼 | 𝐴 ⟩ defined in Example 7.2.2 is thus a coherent presentation of the monoid 𝑀.
